title: Observation and collapse: can a consciousness-linked term be told apart from ordinary noise?
question: Could a consciousness-linked collapse term in a quantum model produce measurement statistics that differ from ordinary environmental dephasing?
reviewedBy: Claude (Anthropic, Opus 5.5), drafted at Chad Holland's direction; human review level: direction only

observations.text: In the simplest paper-faithful case (collapse operators diagonal in the classical-state basis, n = 4), the collapse term equals ordinary dephasing with at most 3 operators: worst superoperator residual 2.13e-14 over 200 random cases. Control with one non-diagonal operator added: minimum residual 3.98e-01.
observations.originator: Claude (Anthropic, Opus 5.5), audit derivation and registered numerical check, 2026-10-22
observations.limitation: Self-tested: it checks the auditor's own derivation for one model class. It says nothing about non-commuting operators or an independently constrained environment, and it is not a study result.

observations.text: 10 of 10 source identity hashes in the literature intake reproduced.
observations.limitation: Checks the identity lines only. The intake's per-source summaries were not audited paper by paper.

adverse.text: For that model class the question is not identifiable against generic environmental dephasing. Telling them apart needs non-commuting collapse operators or an independently constrained environment.

openDecisions.text: The audit recommends REVISE: revise the intake, then a math-only registration, and park any empirical or consciousness-causation arm. Owner decision pending.

nextReview: When the intake is revised or a math-only registration is proposed. Nothing here authorizes a run.
